segments.t: Sigourney Weaver takes a walk across the famous Debilly footbridge in Paris with the Eiffel Tower behind her. While waiting for her secret meeting, she stops to chat with a souvenir seller on the bridge. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Voici la passerelle Debilly à Paris.
Quelle vue magnifique sur la Seine!
Bonjour madame! Regardez mes beaux souvenirs!
Bonjour! Vous avez des tours Eiffel?
Oui, j'ai des petites miniatures.
Elles sont vraiment très mignonnes!
Laquelle préférez-vous? La dorée?
Oui, je prends cette petite tour.
C'est cinq euros, s'il vous plaît.
Tenez, voici un billet de dix.
Merci beaucoup! Vous attendez quelqu'un?
Oui, j'ai un rendez-vous secret.
Attention aux photographes sur le pont!
Merci! Ah, le voilà qui arrive!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Voici la passerelle Debilly à Paris.
'Here is the Debilly footbridge in Paris.' Sigourney walks onto the pedestrian bridge over the river.
Quelle vue magnifique sur la Seine!
'What a magnificent view over the Seine!' Sigourney admires the iconic Parisian panorama.
Bonjour madame! Regardez mes beaux souvenirs!
'Hello ma'am! Look at my beautiful souvenirs!' A street vendor invites her to browse his items.
Bonjour! Vous avez des tours Eiffel?
'Hello! Do you have Eiffel Towers?' Sigourney asks about miniature models of the monument.
Oui, j'ai des petites miniatures.
'Yes, I have small miniatures.' The seller displays his collection of tiny replicas.
Elles sont vraiment très mignonnes!
'They are really very cute!' Sigourney is charmed by the little trinkets.
Laquelle préférez-vous? La dorée?
'Which one do you prefer? The golden one?' The seller offers her a shiny gold version.
Oui, je prends cette petite tour.
'Yes, I will take this little tower.' Sigourney makes her selection from the stand.
C'est cinq euros, s'il vous plaît.
'It is five euros, please.' The vendor tells her the cost of the souvenir.
Tenez, voici un billet de dix.
'Here, take a ten-euro bill.' Sigourney hands over a banknote to pay.
Merci beaucoup! Vous attendez quelqu'un?
'Thank you very much! Are you waiting for someone?' The salesman looks down the walkway.
Oui, j'ai un rendez-vous secret.
'Yes, I have a secret meeting.' Sigourney shares that she is meeting a mystery companion.
Attention aux photographes sur le pont!
'Watch out for photographers on the bridge!' The seller points out paparazzi hiding nearby.
Merci! Ah, le voilà qui arrive!
'Thank you! Ah, here he comes!' Sigourney waves as her companion walks onto the bridge. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Holding her new miniature Eiffel Tower, Sigourney walks forward to greet her guest on the bridge. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'footbridge' and 'view'. You'll catch them now. See you next time!
Bonne journée à Paris!
